text:
maya: FYI Acme (acme-analytics) opened a support case — they're getting 429s from /v1/rerank starting ~11:05 PST. Alert ID RERANK-429-1799998765. Attaching sample request/response below.

support-bot: New alert created: RERANK-429-1799998765 -> ticket #SUP-4812 :rotating_light:

maya: sample curl they sent:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-live-..." \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"query":"best product copy for signup","candidates":[{"id":"c1","text":"Copy A"},{"id":"c2","text":"Copy B"}, ...],"top_k":5}'
```

sample response headers they pasted: ``X-RateLimit-Limit: 120/min, X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0, X-RateLimit-Reset: 17``
response body:```
{ "error": "quota_exceeded", "message": "rate limit exceeded for rerank" }
```

jonah: are they hitting bursts or sustained traffic? Do we have request-id from header (x-request-id)? Also need client SDK version and whether retries/backoff used. :eyes:

maya: they say it started after a small release they rolled last night, traffic pattern shows a sharp spike ~11:02. They included one x-request-id: "req_0a9f7e2b" in logs. SDK: js@2.3.1. They do 8 parallel requests from each worker with 10 workers. No custom backoff (simple immediate retry on 429).

sasha: quick note — rerank counts are heavier (we meter candidate evaluations as cost units). If they send long candidate arrays + retries it can eat quota much faster than plain generation. Did we recently change enforcement rules?

ops-oncall: looking at rate-limit logs now for acct acme-analytics -> I see a spike where many requests returned 429 and the client retried immediately, which produced more requests and doubled consumption. Also noticed a config flip rolled earlier today that tightened per-customer burst window. Timeline: config deploy 10:45, spike 11:02.

jonah: can you paste the raw logs for req_0a9f7e2b? need status codes and any upstream errors.

ops-oncall: raw log snippet:```
[11:02:15] req_0a9f7e2b POST /v1/rerank 200  CPU=0.12s QUOTA_UNITS=45
[11:02:18] req_0a9f7e2b POST /v1/rerank 429  CPU=0.05s QUOTA_UNITS=0
[11:02:18] req_0a9f7e2b retry  POST /v1/rerank 429  CPU=0.05s QUOTA_UNITS=0
[11:02:19] req_0a9f7e2b retry2 POST /v1/rerank 429  CPU=0.04s QUOTA_UNITS=0
```
Observations: retries counted as full requests against burst bucket, and the new window/algorithm didn't clamp retries as we intended.

maya: customer impact: webapp errors, ~10% of requests failing during spike, complain about UX. They've requested an immediate quota bump and root cause.

jonah: short-term mitigation options: 1) give temporary quota bump for acme-analytics; 2) suggest they add exponential backoff (recommended) and cap parallelism; 3) advise moving heavy rerank pipelines to Dedicated capacity if sustained. I'll draft a reply.

sasha: long-term we should change counting so retries that carry the same request-id don't double-count (de-dup at enforcement layer) and add explicit per-candidate metering smoothing. I'll open a tracker.

ops-oncall: actioned temporary quota bump -> increased burst allowance x5 for acme-analytics until EOD. Monitoring set to alert if >80% again. Rolling config change flagged for rollback to previous burst window if we see more regressions.

maya: responding to customer now: told them we've applied a temporary quota bump, suggested reducing concurrency and adding backoff, and asked for a sample failing request-id and SDK call. Also asked if they can deploy a quick client-side backoff patch. :thumbsup:

jonah: repro steps for eng to simulate locally:
```
# simulate 100 clients, each sending 8 parallel rerank requests, each with 50 candidates
python stress_rerank.py --clients 100 --parallel 8 --candidates 50 --duration 60
```
Expect to hit rate limit if burst window < ~5000 candidate-evals/min.

maya: ticket #SUP-4812 updated with temporary bump and links to logs + repro script. Marked P2 and assigned to jonah.

jonah: I'll open PR to add a small server-side de-dupe for retries (check x-request-id) and add metrics around retries counted as quota. If we can't ship quick fix, we should revert today's tighten config.

ops-oncall: I've scheduled a rollback window in case PR can't land before tomorrow. Also creating a short postmortem template to capture timeline + customer impact.

maya: customer said "thanks, that helped for now" and will try backoff patch. I'll follow up after EOD to confirm no recurrence. :raised_hands:

sasha: opened internal tracker RED-8723 "de-dup rerank retry counting + candidate smoothing" and linked to SUP-4812.

jonah: next steps checklist: 1) send customer repro + guidance (maya) 2) keep quota bump until confirmed (ops-oncall) 3) PR for de-dupe + metrics (jonah) 4) postmortem + config rollback if needed (sasha/ops).

maya: noted. closing thread here, will post updates to ticket.
